# CC2 panel review — round 2

Working tree: disposable copy at `.../cdsfl_panel_1x1bm5db/repo`. Reproduction scripts written to `cc2_review_2026-09-02/` in that sandbox (9 scripts + README). One fix applied and validated there.

## Before anything else: the patch cannot be applied as a patch

`git apply` on `fable_scale_review.patch` returns **exit 0 and silently drops 8 files**. They are appended as `=== NEW FILE: path ===` blocks, not diff hunks. After a clean apply:

```
$ ls bench/metering.py scripts/co_discovery_audit.py
ls: bench/metering.py: No such file or directory
ls: scripts/co_discovery_audit.py: No such file or directory
```

757 lines missing, including `bench/metering.py` and 3 of the 5 new test files. In the tree `git apply` produces, both `record_dispatch` call sites sit inside `except Exception: pass`, so **metering is a permanent silent no-op while its comment says "DEFAULT ON"**, and the reproduction command the runner's own docstrings cite three times (`scripts/co_discovery_audit.py --calibrate`) does not exist. Ship it with `git add -N` + `git diff`, or ship the extractor. I wrote one (`extract.py`, 17 lines); everything below is measured on the fully-materialised tree.

---

## Q1 — the rescued patch

### What holds

**The `:.1f` → `:g` fix is sound, and the diagnosis understates the damage.** Verified by execution: `PREREG_GAMMA_PROFILE_THRESHOLDS = (0.5, 0.6, 0.65, 0.7, 0.75, 0.8)`; `.1f` collapses to **4 distinct keys**, `:g` preserves **6**. I checked every archived v3.x report — all 6 have `thresholds` keys `['0.5','0.6','0.7','0.8']` and `gamma_at_lower_edge=None, gamma_at_upper_edge=None, verdict_robust_to_band=None`. **Dead in 6 of 6, exactly as claimed.** The new tests execute `gamma_threshold_profile` against a real archived registry, so this can't regress silently again. Adopt.

**The co-discovery calibration reproduces exactly.** `--calibrate` → 278 labelled cross-model pairs, 42 SAME, 35 links, 30 TP, precision 85.7% [70.6, 93.7], recall 71.4%. I re-derived it by a different route (linking inside each run's own registry, then joining to labels): **25/30 = 83.3% [66.4, 92.7]** — consistent. The corrected numbers survive independent re-derivation. *(My first attempt gave 53.3%; I traced it to a bug in my harness — `str(1)=="True"` is False — not theirs. Recording that because a review that only reports its successful checks is not a review.)*

**The `_handled` guard on the WITHDRAW loop is the right fix** and `TestAWordCannotOverrideATool` is a behavioural test, not a grep. It builds a registry, dispatches two fakes at the real `_post_convergence_sweep`, and asserts the tool's CONFIRMED survives a later prose WITHDRAW. That is the founding principle made executable. Adopt.

### What does not hold

**1. A real test failure, introduced by the patch.** Full suite with `-x`: **1 failed, 2891 passed, 5 skipped.**

```
FAILED test_operational_scripts.py::TestUsageTextAdvertisesOnlyImplementedFlags
       ::test_an_unknown_flag_is_rejected_loudly[co_discovery_audit.py]
```

`calibrate() if "--calibrate" in sys.argv else main()` accepts *any* unknown flag and exits 0 — violating a project contract written 2026-08-30 against exactly this mode ("the 118-day no-op again"). Note the shape: **the patch is green if applied incompletely and red if applied as intended.**

I fixed it (7 lines, argv allow-list). **Fix-validation:**

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `--this-flag-does-not-exist` | exit **0**, ran the full audit | exit **1**, prints usage |
| `--calibrate` | 278/42, 85.7%, 71.4%, exit 0 | **identical**, exit 0 |
| `test_operational_scripts.py` | 1 failed, 120 passed | **121 passed** |

**2. The docstring the correction was written to fix is still wrong.** `link_co_discovery`'s docstring still says *"Measured precision 73.2% [58.1%, 84.3%], recall 52.6% (see constant above)"* — the exact figure the constant **eight lines above** repudiates as reproducing from no committed artefact. The runtime `basis` string is correct; the docstring a reader opens first is not. One-line fix, but this is the second time this number has been wrong in this file.

**3. The operating point is edge-level; the artefact is group-level.** Measured across the archive: 428 edges → 100 groups asserting **610 pairs**. **182 of 610 (29.8%) are in by transitive closure only** — never scored above 0.60. The adjudicated set contains **zero** labelled pairs of that kind, so precision on 30% of what lands in `co_discovery["peers"]` is *unmeasured*, not 85.7%. Worst case: a 12-finding group in `exp40_gate` with direct-edge density 28/66 = 42%. The boilerplate guard killed the 41-finding phantom; it did not remove chaining.

**4. A latent join collision that I checked and which does *not* bite.** `calibrate()` keys entries by `fp.parent.name.split("_")[0]`; 4 prefixes (exp39, exp40, exp42, exp55) cover 12 distinct runs, and `ent.setdefault` binds them to whichever report sorts first. Labelled pairs landing on an ambiguous prefix: **0 of 360.** Right today, fragile tomorrow. One assert, not a retraction.

### `rungs_with_conditions` / `INSTRUCTION_CONDITIONS` — not sound as shipped

Three objections, each measured:

**It has no production caller.** Grepped: only its own test and `scripts/single_model_mode_experiment.py`. `route()` — the sole production entry — still calls `rank_falsifier_writers`. It is dead in the shipping path, so no run artefact will ever record which condition was tried, contra its docstring.

**If wired, it is *shorter* than the ladder it replaces and its strongest rung is unreachable.** Executed with 6 seats on one model:

```
single-model → [('Codex','default'), ('CC2','exec'), ('ChatGPT','adversarial')]   3 rungs
multi-model  → 6 rungs
route(max_rungs=2)  slices to [:2]  →  'adversarial' is NEVER reached
```

A single-model panel gets half the ladder, and loses the rung whose comment calls it the refutation posture.

**The evidence does not transfer.** The +8.7-point result is `codex_exec` vs bare OpenRouter — a different *execution harness* (CLI agent with a tool loop vs an HTTP completion). `INSTRUCTION_CONDITIONS` are three *strings* whose prompt text the function explicitly does not own ("consumed by the caller's `resolve_fn`"). Re-asking one model in different words is not the intervention that produced 25.9% vs 17.3%. To answer the brief's question directly: **as written, it does merely re-ask the same distribution in different words, and the code cannot rule that out because there is no prompt text to inspect.**

The sound version is already in the patch's own vocabulary: make the rung dimension `(seat, api_route)` — `openai/gpt-5.5@codex_exec` vs `openai/gpt-5.5@openrouter`. That is what was actually measured, and `panel_mode_declaration` already keys identity on `model_id@api`.

### "30 of 64" — the arithmetic reproduces exactly, the inference does not survive

I re-ran `link_co_discovery` over all 29 real runs: **100 groups, 64 contain ChatGPT or Codex, 30 contain only one. Exact match.** The number is real.

The inference — "the two conditions find materially different defects" — needs a null, and one is available for free: the same statistic for seat pairs that genuinely *are* different models.

| pair | only-one / either | % |
|---|---:|---:|
| **ChatGPT vs Codex** (same weights) | **30/64** | **46.9%** |
| Gemini vs DeepSeek | 47/81 | 58.0% |
| Gemini vs CC2 | 52/80 | 65.0% |
| Codex vs Gemini | 61/90 | 67.8% |
| ChatGPT vs Gemini | 63/88 | 71.6% |
| Codex vs CC2 | 57/75 | 76.0% |
| ChatGPT vs DeepSeek | 58/76 | 76.3% |
| DeepSeek vs CC2 | 59/74 | 79.7% |
| Codex vs DeepSeek | 68/84 | 81.0% |
| ChatGPT vs CC2 | 61/74 | 82.4% |

**ChatGPT-vs-Codex is the minimum of the matrix.** The two same-weight seats co-discover *more* than any cross-vendor pair — 34/64 = 53% of their groups contain both, the highest in the panel. Read against its own null, the statistic says the opposite of what the comment claims. Threshold sweep 0.40–0.80: the figure moves 32.3%→49.4% but stays below the all-pair median (63–77%) at **every** threshold, so this is not a threshold artefact.

Separately, and as the brief anticipated: at recall 71.4% the matcher misses ~29% of true co-discoveries by construction, which accounts for most of the distance from 0%. The claim was confounded with matcher recall before the null was even applied.

**The claim does not survive. Drop it.** The +8.7-point falsifier-rate result is untouched — it is a direct rate comparison and needs no matcher. Keep that; it remains the strongest empirical thing in the project.

---

## Q2 — the reductio

### It is a broken matcher, and that is provable with no new data

The ratio of the two estimators' *increments* is a closed form in Q2 alone:

```
Chao2bc − S = ((m−1)/m)·Q1(Q1−1)/(2(Q2+1))
jack1   − S = Q1(m−1)/m
ratio       = (Q1−1)/(2(Q2+1)) = 2047/6 = 341
```

The 152× is **arithmetic on Q2=2**. It carries no information about the finding space. At Q1≈2048, **no Q2 below ~314 (15% of Q1) can bring the estimators within 2×, whatever the truth is.** They are not disagreeing about the world; they are both being handed a degenerate sample.

And the matcher is demonstrably the cause. Turning on *one* recording rule moves Q2 from 2 to 64. Rebuilt from `link_co_discovery` groups (unit = group or singleton, occasion = seat, m=5):

| | S | Q1 | Q2 | Chao2bc | jack1 | ratio | completeness |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| as recorded | 2050 | 2048 | **2** | 561,017 | 3,688 | **152×** | 0.37% |
| rebuilt from linker | 1814 | 1714 | **64** | 19,882 | 3,185 | **6.2×** | **9.1%** |

Per-run the ratio tracks Q2 monotonically (Q2=1 → 9.2×; Q2=2 → 15–16×; Q2=6 → 2.5×). Q2 is the whole story. And the rebuild yields **Q3=22, Q4=10, Q5=4** — a plausible decaying incidence tail. Under the recorded schema all three are zero. That tail is precisely what every estimator in this family consumes.

### The minimum recording change

Do not add an estimator. Add one array.

- **Where:** one additive key on the `FindingRegistry` entry, appended at registration **and at every absorption** — `"occasions": [[model, prompt_role, seed, round], …]`. Absorption currently discards this: only `source_aliases` survives, in a format that (as `co_discovery_audit.py` itself documents) records same-model aliases and no cross-model ones. That single discard is what makes Q2=2.
- **Report:** `result["incidence"] = {"occasions": [...], "units": {unit_id: [occasion_idx, …]}, "Q": {1: …, 2: …, 3: …}}`. Sparse; units are the existing canonical ids.
- **Cost — measured on all 29 real archives:** median **832 bytes and 0.017 s per run**; worst case `exp40_gate` (296 findings) **4,357 bytes and 0.267 s**; 33.3 KB across the entire archive. Per *round* that is well under a kilobyte and under a tenth of a second, against a run that costs 69.6 minutes.
- **The part that actually matters:** `occasion = (model, prompt-role, seed, round)` gives you **m from within a single run**. Today m=5 is a hand-typed constant and Q2 can only rise from cross-model repeats. With seeds and rounds as occasions, one run yields dozens of occasions and Q2 rises from within-run repeats too — which is the only way Q2≈300 becomes reachable at all.

### Measuring matcher precision and recall cheaply

The expensive part is truth labels. Three of these buy labels without a human, and one costs nothing at all.

1. **Seeded plants are free ground truth.** The last sim seeded 5 plants and found all 5. Each plant has a known identity ⇒ every same-plant pair is a known SAME, every cross-plant pair a known DIFFERENT. Zero extra dispatches; you already run seeded sims. This buys **recall**, currently the weaker number (71.4% on 42 positives — the Wilson interval on 42 is wide).
2. **Falsifier co-execution as a tool-decided label.** For candidate pair (A,B), run A's falsifier against B's defect and vice versa. Both fire ⇒ same finding, *by the project's own criterion*, decided by execution. Cost: 2 sandbox runs per pair, **no model dispatch**. This is the only labelling scheme here consistent with TOOLS DECIDE, NOT VOTES — the current 85.7% rests on `label_source: counterfactual_repair` and embedding scores.
3. **Fix the population.** The 278 adjudicated pairs were already flagged as candidates by a prior filter. Precision on a candidate-enriched sample is not precision on the all-pairs population the linker sweeps. Cheap correction: draw 100 pairs uniformly from all cross-seat pairs in one run, label by (2), reweight.
4. **A free negative control needing no labels:** invert the cross-seat guard and link *same*-seat pairs only. Same-seat pairs are mostly genuine re-descriptions, so their link rate is a ceiling on what the rule can achieve. **If cross-seat and same-seat rates are equal, the rule is measuring writing style, not defect identity.** One flag, one run of a 1.3-second script.

And report **group-level** precision, since groups are what get written — 29.8% of asserted pairs are currently outside the calibrated population.

---

## Q3 — reuse

The founder is right, and three of the four map cleanly.

**1. `DECOMPOSE_HARD_FLOOR_CHARS` + `decomposed_dispatch` → panel review dispatch. This is the highest-value reuse, and it has a number attached.**

```
rescued patch          77,219 B = 96.5% of DECOMPOSE_HARD_FLOOR_CHARS (80,000)
patch + this brief    ~86,000 B = 108%  of the floor
```

The panel is being handed review payloads that the runner's own policy says **must be chunked**, through a path that does no chunking — which is a mechanical explanation for both timeouts. `should_decompose_v2(label, mgr, payload_chars)` is a pure function taking a char count; wiring it to the review dispatch is a call, not a design. `decomposed_dispatch` already has a `claude_cli` branch.

**2. `build_summary` windowing → the allocator.** `MAX_FULL_DETAIL_OPEN = 20`, `full_detail` / `compact` / `hidden` partition, `hidden_count`, `ACTIVE OVERFLOW` — this is already a budgeted-attention allocator over findings. Map it directly: full-detail = seats/conditions still yielding novel criticals, compact = settled, hidden = refuted. **Reuse the runtime completeness check especially** (`** STATUS PARTITION INCOMPLETE **`). The 2026-08-30 bug it was added for — CORROBORATED in none of the three buckets, invisible to the panel for weeks — is exactly the bug an allocator makes the first time a new seat type isn't in any bucket.

**3. Budget extension → dispatch budget.** Same mechanism, different resource. The need is measured: 10 of 11 archived runs exceed the dispatch budget on their own.

**4. Where the analogy breaks, and it matters.** `decomposed_dispatch` chunks a payload and then **synthesises** — a merge. Panel review must not merge. `link_co_discovery`'s own docstring gets this exactly right: *"two models describing one defect is evidence of CO-DISCOVERY, not evidence the finding is TRUE."* Chunking a review across sub-reviewers and synthesising a consensus is vote-counting with extra steps. **Reuse the chunker; do not reuse the synthesiser.** Each chunk's findings must arrive separately, each carrying its own falsifier.

---

## Q4 — sound or not

**Not yet — but much closer than "0 of 20" makes it sound, and the gap is three specific things, two of which are already written.**

I confirm the premise independently: of 59 archived reports, 11 carry a v3.x `runner_version`, and `_is_simulated` returns **True for all 11**. 0 of 20 is right.

What is genuinely ready: the convergence machinery. I re-read `sim45_postfix` — converged at round 4, `gamma_critical=0.953 ≥ 0.3`, three consecutive zero-new-critical rounds, 5 of 5 plants. It says what the brief says.

What I would not sign, smallest set, with a measurement each:

**(i) The band-sensitivity fix must land.** Dead in 6 of 6 v3.x reports (measured above). Fable's fix is correct. *Fix-validation:* 4 of 6 prereg keys survive `.1f`, 6 of 6 survive `:g`, and the new tests **execute** the profile against a real registry so a key-format regression fails a test instead of emitting nulls. Done — it just needs to be applied completely.

**(ii) Metering is a no-op in the tree the patch produces.** A first paid run under that tree yields zero cost records — the exact artefact the run exists to produce. *Fix-validation available:* re-apply with the extractor and `test_metering_2026-09-02.py` passes (it did — part of the 84 green on the new/changed files). Packaging, not code.

**(iii) The sim seam is untested at the second dispatch primitive, and that is where a paid run differs from every run you have.** `dispatch_to_model` has **no simulation branch at all** — simulation is roster substitution, so real and sim diverge *below* the seam. `decomposed_dispatch` is a separate primitive with 5 API branches; the patch's `_metered` wrapper exists precisely because patching only `dispatch_to_model` missed it. And `should_decompose_v2` forces decomposition above 80K, so **on a real run against a large target the decomposed path is the live path** — the one path the archive has never exercised under v3.x.

The smallest thing that would make me sign: **one paid canary, not an experiment.** Single seat, one round, target deliberately sized above 80,000 chars so the decomposed path is forced. Success = a non-empty metering JSONL with ≥1 record per chunk, and `panel_mode.mode == "single-model"` present in the report. That is cheap, it is not a scaling experiment, and it converts (ii) and (iii) from arguments into measurements.

**One more thing to fix before the first real run:** wire `panel_mode_declaration` — it is the difference between a report that says "six models converged" and one that says what happened. Two edge cases, both confirmed by execution and both one-liners:

```
3 distinct weights, 1 seat lacking a label → seats: 2, mode: 'reduced-diversity'   (a fully diverse panel, mislabelled)
duplicate seat label, 2 weights            → seats: 1, mode: 'reduced-diversity'
same weights, two api routes               → mode: 'single-model' + correct caveat  ✓
```

`MODEL_ROSTER` has 5 distinct labels so neither case fires today — a robustness note, not a defect. The case it was built for works correctly.

## What I did not reach

- **The full suite without `-x` did not finish before I wrote this** — it was at 64% with no failures. What I have: **`-x` run = 1 failed, 2891 passed, 5 skipped in 342 s** (the failure diagnosed and fixed above); the 7 new/changed test files = **84 passed**; `test_operational_scripts.py` post-fix = **121 passed**. I have not verified 4,847 and will not claim it.
- I did not label the 182 transitively-chained pairs — there is zero label coverage for them. That is a data gap, not a time gap, and it is the single biggest hole in the co-discovery operating point.
- I did not implement the incidence recording change. Design and cost are measured; the code is not written.
- I read the 12-file diff in full and the key functions of the 8 extracted files, not every line of all 20.
